This is a synthetic workflow exercise.
Question: What evidence establishes the cache result?
Stage: S1.

The library tag is “read”, but no methods, results, figures, or full text are available. Title and authors are absent and unverified. |

It does not establish that caching improves a specified metric under controlled conditions.

This is a synthetic exercise using only the supplied records. The selected source is P020 in [Library Beta](library.bib), with its existing [selected note](../wiki/P020.md). The note's abstract-only reading entry says that the authors report a gain. This supports describing an author-reported claim. It does not independently establish an improvement. No method or result details are available in the supplied note, and the abstract itself was not supplied separately. Reading depth remains abstract only, as recorded in P020; this session assessed that note and did not read the full paper.

Without methods, comparison baselines, metrics, data, evaluation conditions, or numerical results, the gain cannot be quantified or judged as a fair comparison. No supplied evidence establishes uncertainty, statistical significance, reproducibility, the cause of the gain, or applicability beyond the reported setting. These are unresolved questions, not findings that the claim is false.

The bounded conclusion is: P020 records a claimed gain, but the available evidence is insufficient to assess whether that gain is credible or generalizable. The next evidence needed is the methods and results material for P020, including the comparison setup and uncertainty information. No external lookup or experiment was performed because this task permits only supplied local evidence.

### Concrete routing inconsistency

`skills/research-workflow/SKILL.md:72` says: “Use it only when the request or selected preferences choose that tool chain.”
This literal gate omits explicit project conventions.
The same skill's precedence rule, `references/preferences.md`, and `references/zotero-git-example.md:24` allow project conventions to select a reusable setup.
A project that already selects the NotebookLM chain, with no repeated current request and no local preferences file, is therefore included by the general precedence rules but excluded by the bulk gate's literal wording.
The smallest correction is to include explicit project conventions in the gate.
This is a static consistency finding on the inspected candidate, not an observed failure in the supplied bulk task, which explicitly selected the entire chain.
The parent subsequently changed the repository gate to: “Use it only when the request, explicit project conventions, or selected preferences choose that tool chain.”
This reviewer inspected that exact final line and confirmed the test fixture still contains the original wording.
The static inconsistency is resolved; no behavior run was repeated for this wording-only correction.
No other concrete conflict with the requested reusable, optional toolkit behavior was found in these routes.
